paper_title: Aryl-Aryl Bond Formation by Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Direct Arylation

key_components.ligand: Phosphines (e.g., PPh3, trialkylphosphines, Buchwald biphenylphosphines), N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs)
key_components.additive: Phase-transfer catalysts (e.g., n-Bu4NBr), Silver salts (e.g., Ag2CO3, AgOTf) to mitigate iodide inhibition
key_components.electrophile: Aryl halides (I, Br, Cl) and pseudohalides (OTf)
key_components.nucleophile: Unactivated aryl or heteroaryl C-H bonds
key_components.solvent: Polar aprotic solvents (DMF, DMA, NMP, DMSO) or nonpolar solvents (toluene, xylene)

mechanistic_insights: The mechanism of C-H insertion is highly system-dependent and can proceed via several pathways, including electrophilic aromatic substitution (SEAr), concerted metalation-deprotonation (CMD), σ-bond metathesis, or Heck-type carbometalation.

Regioselectivity is a major challenge in intermolecular reactions and is typically controlled by either the inherent electronics of the arene or, more commonly, by a coordinating directing group (e.g., amides, ketones, pyridines) that forms a metallacycle intermediate.
In unsymmetrical substrates with directing groups, arylation typically occurs at the less sterically hindered ortho position.

For some systems, particularly intramolecular reactions, iodide anions generated from aryl iodide substrates can act as catalyst inhibitors. This can be overcome by using silver salt additives (e.g., Ag2CO3).

Large primary kinetic isotope effects (kH/kD > 1) are often observed, suggesting that C-H bond cleavage is involved in the rate-determining step, which argues against a simple SEAr mechanism in many cases.

quantitative_outcomes.best_performing_conditions: As a review, many high-yielding conditions are reported. A representative example for intramolecular arylation is the use of 0.1 mol% Pd(OAc)2 with a phosphine ligand (31), K2CO3 in DMA at 145 °C, which gave 96% yield (Scheme 86).
quantitative_outcomes.notes: This is a comprehensive review from 2007 covering the state-of-the-art in transition-metal-catalyzed direct arylation for aryl-aryl bond formation. It discusses a wide scope of inter- and intramolecular reactions involving both aryl and heteroaryl C-H bonds, with extensive details on reaction conditions, directing groups, regioselectivity, and proposed mechanistic pathways.
